points.name: settings.sound.dnd_register
points.interpretation: Registers the common action callback with event filter 7 and user data 0 for the disturb.settings row.

points.name: settings.sound.vibration_toggle_register
points.interpretation: Registers the common action callback with event filter 7 and user data 1 for vibrate_mode.settings.

points.name: settings.sound.vibration_mode_register
points.interpretation: Registers the common action callback with event filter 7 and user data 2 for vibrate_mode_display.settings.

points.name: settings.sound.action_id
points.interpretation: The callback interprets 0 as opening the disturb settings path, 1 as toggling the vibration setting, and 2 as opening the vibration mode path when allowed.

points.name: settings.vibration.selection_register
points.interpretation: A two-iteration builder registers the same selection callback for filter 7, passing 0 and 1 as user data.

points.name: settings.vibration.selection_data
points.interpretation: The callback uses the registered value as a bound while searching option objects; expected values are 0 or 1, not an unrestricted integer.

points.name: settings.vibration.selection_target
points.interpretation: The callback compares the current event target against the option controls and selects a standard or enhanced mode path.

points.name: settings.vibration.confirm_event_code
points.interpretation: The enhancement confirmation callback applies mode 2 and sends updates only when event code equals 7.

evidence: The settings app manifest registers both page descriptors. Each page creates and clears its allocated state. The sound page registers a common callback for three rows, with distinct user-data values. The vibration page builds two options and registers the selection callback with values 0 and 1; the callback also compares the current target to the option objects. The enhancement dialog invokes a separate event-code handler.
scope: Only the listed call sites while the respective page state is present. Other paths that change vibration, sound or do-not-disturb settings are not intercepted.
limitations: Values outside the observed registration domains may lead to invalid option accesses. Changing behavior can desynchronize UI and persisted settings. Page state is not a thread barrier; shared-entry publication and rollback require system-wide quiescence. Device behavior is unverified.
